threads: Standings after Wk 7: FBT and Ligers 6-1; E720 and Wad 5-2; Viva, Wet Bandits and BMB 4-3; DD 3-4; Bloodfeast and Scally 2-5; Nuts 1-6; Prestige 0-7.
Streaks: FBT W6, BMB W4, Ligers W3, Wad W1; Nuts L6, Prestige L7, Viva L2, E720 L1 (5-game streak snapped), Bloodfeast L1.
Bloodfeast: Wk 7 low 462 (penalty). Optimal only 479.25. Started Kenyon Sadiq (4.50) after the Wk 6 preview said whoever starts Sadiq loses. Jaylin Noel 105.25 -> -2.25. Series vs FBT now 13-10.
FBT: six straight. Dak Prescott 123, Tre Tucker 102.25 (third straight big week), CMC 90.25.
E720: perfect-lineup run over. Geno Smith 127.75 bench, Tanner McKee started 63.25. Opt 709.25 would have won. Jaylen Wright ($953) bench, 4.00.
DD: JSN 169, week's top player. Benched Bo Nix 137 and Quinshon Judkins 104 (the week after starting Judkins for a DNP). Opt 819.75. Snapped L3.
FAAB: Ligers and DD $1,000 untouched; E720 $0; Bloodfeast $40.
Ligers: beat Prestige by 3.00, week's closest. Cousins 116.75, Amon-Ra 139.25. Started Daniel Jones too (23.50).
Prestige: 0-7. Michael Penix Jr. 112.75 bench, Kyler Murray started 77, Ted Hurst started 0.00. Opt 608.25 wins by 54.
Nuts: Tony Pollard 159 on bench; opt 823.75 was the best possible lineup in the league; lost by 10.25. Second straight week benching 100+. Series vs BMB 7-12.
BMB: 0-3 to 4-3, week high 691.5. Luther Burden 126, Maye 148.25. Malik Willis 135.5 bench.
Scally: snapped L5. Started Bucky Irving, he scored 106. 3-0 all-time vs Viva.
Viva: second straight optimal-or-close loss (577.75/577.75). Burrow 159; Henry 25.50 after 20.50.
Wad: league-high PF 4,801.75. Javonte Williams 127.5, McBride 108.25, Deshaun Watson 101.5. Series vs Wet Bandits 8-5.
Wet Bandits: 491.5, second-lowest. Mahomes 38.25. Even opt 530.75 loses by 160.

Wk 7 moves: Bloodfeast $751 J.J. McCarthy (bid raised from $680), cut Dylan Sampson for Christian Kirk (0.00); Viva cut Jalen Hurts for Mike Gesicki; BMB $58 Demario Douglas (WB cut him last week); WB $31 Mumpfield, $1 Roschon Johnson; Nuts FA Tyler Huntley 90.5; E720 dropped Mark Andrews for Michael Mayer; FBT cut Jameis Winston, added Bam Knight; Ligers added Adonai Mitchell.

takes.0005: Six straight. Full Blown Trash didn't need the week's best score; they just needed Bloodfeast to show up, which was generous of everyone involved. Dak Prescott (123) and Tre Tucker (102.25, his third straight monster game) did most of the work, Christian McCaffrey added 90.25 and Josh Jacobs 84.25, and the final was 647.5–462, a 185.5-point margin against a team whose best possible lineup still loses by 168. Tyler Higbee started again and scored 10.50, which is now a tradition. They also cut Jameis Winston, their $200 backup who kept outscoring the starters from the bench, and picked up Bam Knight, who started for 35.25. 6-1, tied for first, and next up is 720 in the game that decides who's actually the best team in this league.
takes.0001: A week after winning the Basement Bowl, Bloodfeast spent $751 of its FAAB on J.J. McCarthy, raising its own bid from $680 at the last minute. McCarthy scored 63.50. Then they scored 462, the lowest in the league, and gets to make a donation to the bitcoin pool. Jaylin Noel went from 105.25 to -2.25. Negative. Christian Kirk, picked up off waivers for Dylan Sampson (last week's $115 buy), started and scored 0.00. Isaiah Likely, 105.25 last week, scored 9. And Kenyon Sadiq started and scored 4.50, a week after this very publication wrote, in print, that whoever starts Kenyon Sadiq loses. KC Concepcion (108.25) and Puka Nacua (81) tried. The optimal lineup was 479.25, so there's no one to blame but the roster. 2-5, $40 left in the bank, and the series lead over Trash is down to 13-10.
takes.0002: Two perfect lineups this season. This week, 130.5 points on the bench and a loss. Geno Smith scored 127.75 on the bench while Tanner McKee, last week's free-agent miracle, started and scored 63.25. Malachi Fields (62.25) and Kaelon Black (43.5) watched from the bench too, and the optimal lineup, 709.25, wins this game by 86. CeeDee Lamb (105.5) and Jameson Williams (118.25) showed up. The front office also dropped Mark Andrews for Michael Mayer, who started and scored 24. Jaylen Wright, the $953 bench ornament, scored 4.00, so at least he stayed in character. The five-game streak is over, 720 is 5-2, and the next opponent is Trash, the only team in the league that's actually better.
takes.0012: The Diamond Dogs beat the league leaders while benching 241 points. Bo Nix scored 137 on the bench. Quinshon Judkins, who started last week and never played, sat this week and scored 104. Of course he did. Jaxon Smith-Njigba didn't care: 169 points, the best individual game of the week, plus D'Andre Swift (73), Sam Darnold (82.75) and Ja'Marr Chase (71.5). Final: 623.25–578.75. The optimal lineup was 819.75, which would have been the best score in the league by 128. The losing streak is over, the series with 720 is 12-6, and the Diamond Dogs are 3-4 and annoyed with themselves in a new way.
takes.0003: The Ligers beat Prestige by three points. Three. 554.25–551.25, the closest game of the week, against a team that hasn't won all year and benched its best quarterback. Kirk Cousins (116.75) is now officially the guy, Amon-Ra St. Brown went for 139.25, and Jonathan Taylor added 83.75. Daniel Jones also started, and scored 23.50, so the quarterback debate from last week has been settled by playing both of them and only one of them showing up. 6-1, tied for first, three straight. Not every win has to be pretty. This one wasn't even close to pretty. They also picked up Adonai Mitchell, now on his third team in two weeks. Next: BMB, the hottest team in the league.
takes.0010: Prestige lost by three. They benched Michael Penix Jr., who scored 112.75, and started Kyler Murray, who scored 77. They also started Ted Hurst, who scored 0.00. Either fix wins the game. The optimal lineup, 608.25, wins it by 54. Matthew Stafford (97.25), Colston Loveland (76.75) and Braelon Allen (74.5) did their part against the 6-1 defending champs and got nothing for it. 0-7, the only winless team in the league, and the first close game they've played all year ended with the manager costing them. Next up is Nuts, also very bad. Somebody has to win that one. Probably.
takes.0011: BMB was 0-3. BMB is 4-3, the week's high scorer at 691.5, and the hottest team in the league for a second straight week. Drake Maye (148.25) keeps throwing, Luther Burden broke out for 126, Malik Nabers added 83.25 and Tucker Kraft 61. They also paid $58 for Demario Douglas, the receiver the Wet Bandits bought for $31 and cut a week ago. He scored 17.25. They beat Nuts by 10.25 and left Malik Willis's 135.5 on the bench, which they can get away with because Nuts left even more. Four straight, three of them over 690. The series with Nuts is now 12-7. Next up: the Ligers, 6-1, who just needed a miracle to beat Prestige. BMB doesn't look like they need miracles anymore.
takes.0006: Nuts lost by 10.25 with Tony Pollard's 159 on the bench. One hundred fifty-nine. The optimal lineup was 823.75, the best possible score of any team this week, and they lost. Last week they benched Omar Cooper Jr.'s 102.25; this week they started him (111.25) and benched someone else's career game instead. Zay Flowers (127.75), free-agent pickup Tyler Huntley (90.5), Emanuel Wilson (86.25) and Cam Skattebo (84.75, up from 0.00) all delivered. 681.25 is a winning score in four of the six games this week. Not this one. Six straight losses, 1-6, and Prestige is next, which at least guarantees one of them wins.
takes.0008: Wad of Hell got embarrassed by BMB last week and responded by scoring 690.5, the second-best score of the week, behind BMB. Javonte Williams (127.5), Trey McBride (108.25) and, somehow, Deshaun Watson (101.5) led the way, Jordan Love added 98.5 and Bijan Robinson got back to 75.75. Nico Collins started and scored 4.50, Jalen Coker 6.75, and they won by 199 anyway. The series with the Wet Bandits is now 8-5. Back to 5-2, tied for third, and quietly the highest-scoring team in the league at 4,801.75. Next up is Resistance, who have lost two straight.
takes.0004: The Wet Bandits scored 491.5, the second-lowest score of the week, and even the optimal lineup (530.75) loses by 160. Tee Higgins (136) and Caleb Williams (126) combined for 262. The other eight starters combined for 229.5. Patrick Mahomes scored 38.25. Juwan Johnson started again and scored 5.25, a big improvement over last week's 0.00. Roschon Johnson ($1 on waivers) started for 6.50, and Konata Mumpfield ($31) for 11.25. Kenneth Walker III gave back his 122.25 from last week and scored 33.75. 4-3, and next up are the Scallywags, who just won their first game in a month and are feeling good about it.
takes.0007: The curse is lifted. The Scallywags started Bucky Irving and he scored 106. Rhamondre Stevenson (105.75) and Jared Goff (105.25) also cleared 100, C.J. Stroud added 86.25 and Ollie Gordon II 76.5, and the Scallywags beat Resistance 652.75–577.75 to end a five-game losing streak. Darren Waller scored 62.5 on the bench and Jahan Dotson started for 4.50, so it wasn't a perfect week, but nobody's complaining. They're 3-0 all-time against Resistance. 2-5, still bad, but a lot less bad than last week. Next: the Wet Bandits.
takes.0009: Resistance set a perfect lineup, 577.75 of 577.75, and lost by 75. Two straight weeks where the bench couldn't have saved them. Joe Burrow (159) was brilliant. Nobody else was. Derrick Henry scored 25.50 a week after 20.50, A.J. Brown 36, Keenan Allen 23.25, and the receiver room continues to be a place where points go to die. Also this week: Resistance cut Jalen Hurts. For Mike Gesicki. Gesicki started and scored 29.50. The Scallywags, who hadn't won since September, beat them comfortably and are now 3-0 all-time in the series. Two weeks ago this team was 4-1. Now it's 4-3, losing two straight, with Wad of Hell up next.

dispatch.head: Trash and the Ligers reach 6-1, and 720 gets left behind
dispatch.dek: Full Blown Trash and the Ligers are 6-1. Entertainment 720 and Wad of Hell are 5-2. Resistance, the Wet Bandits and BMB are 4-3. The Diamond Dogs are 3-4, Bloodfeast and the Scallywags are 2-5, Nuts are 1-6, and Prestige is 0-7. The trade deadline is Thursday at 8:15 p.m.

dispatch.head: The Diamond Dogs bench 241 points and still beat 720
dispatch.dek: Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored 169, the best game of the week, and the Diamond Dogs won 623.25–578.75 with Bo Nix (137) and Quinshon Judkins (104) on the bench. 720 left Geno Smith's 127.75 on its own bench. That ended 720's five-game winning streak.

dispatch.head: Nuts bench Tony Pollard's 159 and lose by 10
dispatch.dek: Nuts' optimal lineup was 823.75, the best possible score in the league this week. They scored 681.25 and lost to BMB, 691.5–681.25. It's their second straight week benching a 100-point player and their sixth straight loss.

dispatch.head: Prestige benches Penix, starts a zero and loses to the champs by three
dispatch.dek: Michael Penix Jr. scored 112.75 on the bench and Ted Hurst started for 0.00. The Ligers won 554.25–551.25, the closest game of the week. Prestige's optimal lineup would have won by 54. Prestige is 0-7.

dispatch.head: Bloodfeast spends $751, scores 462, and yes, starts Kenyon Sadiq
dispatch.dek: Last week's preview said whoever starts Kenyon Sadiq loses. Bloodfeast started him (4.50), paid $751 for J.J. McCarthy (63.50), watched Jaylin Noel went from 105.25 to -2.25, and Trash won 647.5–462 for its sixth straight. Bloodfeast's optimal lineup was 479.25. The penalty goes in the bitcoin pool.

dispatch.kick: Week 7 · Hottest Team in the League
dispatch.head: BMB has gone 0-3 to 4-3, and the Ligers are next
dispatch.dek: Drake Maye (148.25) and Luther Burden (126) led BMB to the week's high score, 691.5. BMB has won four straight and topped 690 in three of them. Wad of Hell bounced back right behind them at 690.5, beating the Wet Bandits by 199.

dispatch.head: Bloodfeast spends $751 on J.J. McCarthy, and Resistance cuts Jalen Hurts
dispatch.dek: Bloodfeast raised its own bid from $680 to $751 and has $40 left. McCarthy scored 63.50. Resistance cut Hurts for Mike Gesicki (29.50). BMB paid $58 for Demario Douglas, a week after the Wet Bandits cut him. The trade deadline is Thursday at 8:15 p.m.

dispatch.head: Bucky Irving starts and scores 106, and the Scallywags finally win
dispatch.dek: Irving, Rhamondre Stevenson and Jared Goff all scored over 100 in a 652.75–577.75 win that ended a five-game losing streak. Resistance set a perfect lineup and still lost. The Scallywags are 3-0 all-time against Resistance.

Team of the Week.text: 691.5, the week's top score and a fourth straight win. A team that started 0-3 has topped 690 in three of its last four games.

Biggest Bust.text: Tony Pollard scored 159 on the bench. The optimal lineup was 823.75, the best possible score of anyone in the league. Nuts lost by 10.25.

Luckiest Win.text: Won by 3.00 against a winless team that benched a 112.75-point quarterback and started a receiver who scored 0.00.

0005-0002.head: Game of the Week: the two best teams in the league
0005-0002.text: Trash (6-1) has won six straight and allowed 3,453.25 points, 579 fewer than anyone else. 720 (5-2) is 0.50 behind Trash in points scored and just lost with 130.5 points on its bench. Trash leads the series 12-7, but the last three games were decided by 50, 8.75 and 3.5 points; last year's opener went 498.25–494.75. Dak Prescott, Tre Tucker and Christian McCaffrey are rolling. 720 has Jahmyr Gibbs, CeeDee Lamb and Jameson Williams, plus a quarterback question: Geno Smith (127.75) or Tanner McKee? With $0 of FAAB and the trade deadline Thursday night, 720 is stuck with what it has.

0003-0011.head: The champs run into the hottest team in the league
0003-0011.text: The Ligers (6-1) needed a three-point escape against Prestige. BMB (4-3) has won four straight and scored 691.5 or more in three of them. The Ligers lead the series 12-8, but these games stay close: BMB won 613.5–610.75 in 2024, and the Ligers took last year's 691.5–633.25. Drake Maye, Luther Burden and Malik Nabers against Kirk Cousins, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jonathan Taylor. If BMB benches Malik Willis again, they'd better be right.

0009-0008.head: Resistance needs a win before it's a slide
0009-0008.text: Resistance (4-3) has lost two straight, and it wasn't the lineups' fault either time. Wad of Hell (5-2) just scored 690.5 and leads the series 11-9. Their 2023 game was 748.25–733. Joe Burrow (159) is carrying Resistance, while Derrick Henry has 46 points over two weeks. Wad brings Javonte Williams, Trey McBride, Jordan Love and Bijan Robinson. For Wad, Nico Collins has to show up for more than 4.50.

0001-0012.head: Bloodfeast tries to stop paying the pool
0001-0012.text: Bloodfeast (2-5) just posted the week's low score. The Diamond Dogs (3-4) benched 241 points and still beat 720. Bloodfeast leads the series 10-9 and has won the last three, including 744.75–518 last year. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (169) is the best player on the field. The Diamond Dogs' real opponent is their own bench: Bo Nix and Quinshon Judkins combined for 241 there. KC Concepcion and Puka Nacua need help from anyone on Bloodfeast, including a tight end who isn't Kenyon Sadiq.

0007-0004.head: The Scallywags try to build a streak
0007-0004.text: The Scallywags (2-5) finally won, with Bucky Irving, Rhamondre Stevenson and Jared Goff all over 100. The Wet Bandits (4-3) scored 491.5 and are 1-1 against them all-time: the Scallywags won 634.75–514.5 in 2024, and the Wet Bandits took last year's 482.5–451. Tee Higgins and Caleb Williams scored 262 of the Wet Bandits' 491.5. Patrick Mahomes (38.25) and Kenneth Walker III (33.75) need to give them some help.

0010-0006.head: Somebody has to win this one
0010-0006.text: Prestige (0-7) visits Nuts (1-6), who have lost six straight. Between them, they benched 271.75 points last week: Michael Penix Jr. (112.75) and Tony Pollard (159), each of which would have won his game. Nuts lead the series 12-6, but Prestige won last year's game 714.75–614.25. Zay Flowers, Omar Cooper Jr. and Ashton Jeanty face Matthew Stafford, Colston Loveland and George Pickens. The loser has the worst record in the league to itself.
